title: Ashenvale
body: Ashenvale is the great forest of the night elves, a land of towering ancient trees south of Darkshore and Felwood, reaching down to the Barrens and the Stonetalon Mountains. After the Sundering the kaldorei rebuilt their society beneath its boughs, and for long ages the Sentinels patrolled its shadows while the druids slept. The Third War broke that peace. Grom Hellscream's Warsong orcs came to the forest, clashed with the Sentinels, and in a rage not wholly their own slew the demigod Cenarius. Grom later redeemed his honor by helping Thrall destroy the pit lord Mannoroth. The Warsong still cut the forest's timber, and the Silverwing Sentinels fight the Warsong Outriders for every grove. The Alliance holds Astranaar and Maestra's Post, and draenei help restore Forest Song, while the Horde holds Splintertree Post and Zoram'gar on the coast. Around them the furbolg tribes have turned savage, satyrs haunt old ruins, naga swarm the Zoram Strand, the Forsaken defile a barrow den, and remnants of the Burning Legion linger in the east.

title: Maestra's Post
body: Maestra's Post is a small night elf camp of a tower and a large hall on the road through western Ashenvale, and an unusual meeting place. Two humans live here: the paladin Delgren the Purifier, who helps the Sentinels wherever demons or undead are found, and Feero Ironhand, who carries Delgren's supplies and messages north to Auberdine, though cult assassins and undead lurk along the road. The herbalist Orendil Broadleaf brews his remedies here. Liladris Moonriver waits for the drowsy druid Kerlonian Evershade to find his way down from Darkshore, and Sentinel Onaeya awaits word of Aynasha, a Sentinel sent toward Auberdine whom furbolg trackers ambushed and poisoned on the way.

title: Ordil'Aran and Bathran's Haunt
body: North of Maestra's Post, toward the Darkshore border, two old ruins stand in the woods. At the Ruins of Ordil'Aran the warlocks of the Cult of the Dark Strand have made camp. Cultists, adepts and a frenzied enforcer guard excavators who dig among the stones, and one of them carried a soul gem said to hold the secret of the cult's power. A little farther north lies Bathran's Haunt, where a plant called Bathran's Hair once grew, known for curing ailments of the spirit. The Forsaken now prowl those ruins, seekers, herbalists and thugs moving among the stones, and the night elves find their presence deeply troubling.

title: The Zoram Strand
body: The Zoram Strand is the long northwestern shore of Ashenvale. Beneath its waves lies Zoram, a night elf city destroyed in the Sundering and swallowed by the sea, lost and nearly forgotten for ages. Now the naga have returned to it, for reasons no one knows. Wrathtail myrmidons, sorceresses, sea witches and wave riders crowd the beaches among crawlers and hydras, a naga called Lady Vespia is sometimes seen among them, and their leader Ruuzel keeps an isle on the northern edge of the drowned city. Offshore the naga keep a brazier burning in honor of the hydra Vorsha. North of Zoram'gar, Fallenroot satyrs and tide priestesses watch over the entrance to Blackfathom Deeps.

title: Zoram'gar Outpost
body: Zoram'gar Outpost is the Horde's foothold on the western coast of Ashenvale, a camp of orcs and Darkspear trolls on the Zoram Strand. Karang Amakkar calls it the front line of the Horde's conquest of the forest and sends fighters against the furbolgs who stand between this coast and Splintertree Post. Naga raids are frequent, and the hydra Vorsha the Lasher has struck the camp again and again without provocation, until Muglash resolved to draw her out by putting out the naga's brazier. Marukai wants the naga thrown back into the depths, the troll Mitsuwa grieves for kin killed by Thistlefur furbolgs on their way here, and Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring studies the waters and the deeps nearby.

title: Thistlefur Village
body: North of Astranaar and east of the Zoram Strand lies Thistlefur Village, home of the Thistlefur furbolgs, who outnumber even the fierce Foulweald. The furbolgs were not always enemies of the night elves, but the Thistlefur have grown corrupt and savage, and their numbers have swelled so fast that Raene Wolfrunner fears they may soon dare to attack Astranaar itself. Their chieftain is Dal Bloodclaw, and the brute Rorgish Jowl prowls among them. At the far end of the village is Thistlefur Hold, a cave where the tribe keeps its plunder, including sacred charms taken from slain trolls. The Thistlefur even caged Ruul Snowhoof here, having mistaken him for a bear.

title: Astranaar
body: Astranaar is the chief night elf town of Ashenvale, built on an island in a lake and joined to the shore by bridges where the main road passes through. Travelers find an inn, a hippogryph roost and a shelf of old histories. Raene Wolfrunner and her wolf Dagri direct the struggle against the furbolgs, while Shindrell Swiftfire sends fighters against the naga of the Zoram Strand and reports to Kayneth Stillwind at Forest Song. Faldreas Goeth'Shael listens to the forest spirits, Sentinel Thenysil frets over a friend sent to Stonetalon, and the draenei paladin Vindicator Palanaar has come to aid her new allies. In one house, Pelturas Whitemoon keeps watch over his gravely ill daughter.

title: The Shrine of Aessina
body: In the woods of western Ashenvale, between Maestra's Post and the Fire Scar Shrine, lies a shrine dedicated to Aessina, a spirit of the wilderness. It is a quiet glade where night elf hunters train and buy their supplies, and where a spirit healer guides the fallen back to the living. Here Therysil waits for news of her wandering sister Therylune, who strayed as far as the Master's Glaive in Darkshore and had to be rescued from its cultists before word of her safety could reach the shrine. The peace is uneasy. Felguards and felslayers from the Fire Scar Shrine to the south prowl near the edge of the glade.

title: Fire Scar Shrine
body: In southwestern Ashenvale lies the Fire Scar Shrine, a place of great evil where demons walk openly beneath the trees. Felslayers and lesser felguards hold the ground, and a demon called Akkrilus is sometimes found among them. Their master is Ilkrud Magthrull, a powerful orc warlock who makes his home here. Delgren the Purifier of Maestra's Post long counted him little more than an annoyance and left him alone, until the hunt for the Cult of the Dark Strand led to his door. The fel creatures do not keep to the shrine: a few prowl north as far as the edge of the Shrine of Aessina's quiet glade.

title: Iris Lake
body: Iris Lake lies east of Astranaar along the road through central Ashenvale. On its isle rests Elune's Tear, a stone found in no other place and said to wash away corruption. Shadethicket moss eaters wander its shores, with a rarely seen creature called Branch Snapper among them. A little beyond the lake, up a quiet path north of the road, the dryad Shael'dryn tends a moonwell. She refuses to leave the forest or give it up to corruption, and she once knew the secrets of the treants who guarded part of an old wizard's rod, before they too were twisted.

title: The Ruins of Stardust
body: South of Astranaar, near the mountains that divide Ashenvale from Stonetalon, the Ruins of Stardust stand in a lake, once a holy place of the night elves. A small fountain at the center of the lake still gives water so pure that shamans of the Horde seek it out for their rites. Bushes dusted with a frosted powder grow among the stones, and that stardust is said to cool a raging fever. The ruins are not undefended. Old tales warned that great creatures of nature guard them against visitors, and Shadethicket raincallers and wood shapers do indeed roam the water.

title: Mystral Lake
body: Mystral Lake is the largest lake in Ashenvale, lying in the south of the forest not far from the tunnel of the Talondeep Path. Its waters have turned against all who come near: befouled water elementals rise from it, and one called Tideress bears a glowing globe of the filth within. On the northern shore a small Sentinel camp, the Silverwind Refuge, keeps trainers and merchants, and there Sentinel Velene Starstrike traced the elementals to Sarilus Foulborne, an undead mage of the Barrens. the Horde has its eye on a gazebo on the lake that looks over the camp, and on the high ground to the southeast lives Krolg, an old furbolg untouched by corruption.

title: Fallen Sky Lake
body: Fallen Sky Lake is a small lake in southeastern Ashenvale with an island at its heart. The night elves once came here to gather moonstones, fallen stones holding a power that could give back strength the body had lost. Then the Shadethickets came. Stone movers and bark rippers now roam the shore, and their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, has gathered every fallen moonstone and hoards them on the island. He will give them up only in death.

title: Raynewood Retreat
body: In the heart of Ashenvale, Raynewood Retreat surrounds a great tree of the same name. Cenarion protectors and vindicators, Sentinels and the dryads called laughing sisters guard its glades, while blink dragons flit through the branches. At the top of the tree hides Keeper Ordanus, one of the eldest sons of the forest god Cenarius, spirited here in secret from Stonetalon Peak. He has not escaped his enemy. Braelyn Firehand, who serves a master in Jaedenar and hates the druids for stifling her magic, has seen his hiding place by that magic and wants his head. Elsewhere in the retreat prowls the nightsaber Shadumbra, feared by every Horde traveler bound west for the Zoram Strand.

title: The Howling Vale
body: In northern Ashenvale, near the Felwood border, a cave holds the ruined Shrine of Mel'Thandris, where an old inscription still asks Elune to shine upon the vale and light the ways of the forest forever. Wolf-men fill it now. Terrowulf fleshrippers and shadow weavers prowl the cave under a Packlord, and their chilling calls gave the vale its name. The shrine keeps the Tome of Mel'Thandris, a book that is no true book: its leaves were blessed by Mel'Thandris herself and record events of import. Its visions led the Sentinels to the Scythe of Elune, and the journal of the priestess Velinde Starsong tells that she sent her worgen here to wait.

title: Xavian
body: Xavian is a satyr stronghold in northeastern Ashenvale, west of Forest Song, raised among the ruins of an old night elf temple. Xavian felsworn, hellcallers, rogues and betrayers fill its camps, and they work their foul rites with oil seized from a Warsong delivery. One of them, Geltharis, took the Branch of Cenarius, a relic the dryads of the forest set out to win back. The sisters who came searching for it did not return, and the one who led them, Anilia, was found near the ruins, dying of a terrible wound.

title: Satyrnaar and Night Run
body: Satyrnaar was once a shrine of the night elves, where pilgrims came to feel the healing power of the Chalice of Elune, a relic entrusted to its keepers by the priests of the goddess. Today Bleakheart satyrs camp among its ruins with a satyr called Prince Raze, and the very wood of the place has been fouled. Yet the chalice lay there still, its light undimmed after all the years of corruption around it. To the west, the Felmusk satyrs hold Night Run. In both camps the Cult of the Dark Strand hid a soul gem binding trapped Highborne spirits, and the satyrs kept them in their blood-soaked temples.

title: Splintertree Post
body: Splintertree Post is the Horde's chief outpost in Ashenvale, raised by Grom Hellscream's Warsong clan when the orcs first came into the forest during the Third War. It stands in the east, north of the road from the Barrens, and Splintertree guards stand watch around it. Most of its people are orcs and tauren, though a goblin trader, Pixel, has stopped here on her way to Ratchet, and blood elves have come to cement their place among the Horde. Mastok Wrilehiss watches the caravans and dislikes everyone, Senani Thunderheart calls hunters to the Ashenvale Hunt, Locke Okarr keeps the lumber camps supplied, and Ertog Ragetusk sends raiders against Silverwing Outpost.

title: Silverwing Outpost
body: Silverwing Outpost is a Sentinel stronghold in the forest southwest of Splintertree Post, held by Silverwing sentinels and warriors under the command of Duriel Moonfire, a night elf with a fierce reputation. It stands uncomfortably close to the Horde. Ashenvale outrunners slip out from here to spy on the Horde's defenses, and the orcs of Splintertree hunt them through the woods to keep the Alliance blind. The orcs plan worse. The Warsong raider Torek has gathered his warriors to storm the outpost and cut down its leader, hoping to win a few good scars in the fight.

title: The Dor'Danil Barrow Den
body: South of Splintertree Post lies the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, long a resting place of night elf druids. The Horde's advance left it behind enemy lines, and then the Forsaken came. They made a camp beside it to brew poisons and diseases in bottles, and the druids who slept within were murdered, their spirits torn from their bodies and driven mad. Severed sleepers, dreamers and keepers haunt the barrows with their former leaders Taneel Darkwood, Uthil Mooncall and Mavoris Cloudsbreak, and rotting slimes devour whatever they find. Forsaken assassins and the Darkslayer Mordenthal still prowl the camp, and the hippogryph Sharptalon hunts the hills nearby.

title: Warsong Lumber Camp
body: In eastern Ashenvale the Warsong clan fells the ancient trees on a scale the night elves can hardly bear to watch. Peons and Horde deforesters work under Overseer Gorthak, shredders bought in Ratchet tear through the trunks, and grunts, shamans and scouts guard the cutting. A second Warsong labor camp to the southwest, near Fallen Sky Lake, does the same work. To the night elves of Forest Song, just to the north, the camps are a blight upon the forest, and they strike at them often. The camps have other enemies too: demons from Felfire Hill raid them, and satyrs and furbolgs have plundered their supplies.

title: Forest Song
body: Forest Song is an old night elf outpost in the Nightsong Woods of northeastern Ashenvale. For a long time its only resident was the druid Kayneth Stillwind, who feared he might be the last of his people to see these lands before their fall. The kaldorei have invited the draenei to share in restoring it, and under Architect Nemos and Vindicator Vedaar of the Hand of Argus tents are rising where buildings will one day stand. Nemos will not fell the grove's ancient trees, so the ancient of war Gnarl purifies timber taken from the Warsong loggers and from Satyrnaar. Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper keeps watch against satyrs, orcs and the demons of Felfire Hill.

title: Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Canyon
body: In Demon Fall Canyon, in southeastern Ashenvale, Grom Hellscream and Thrall faced the pit lord Mannoroth, who had first cursed the orcs with his blood. Grom struck the demon down and died in the blast of its death, and with Mannoroth gone the blood curse was ended. A monument raised by Thrall marks the place where Grom lies, and Mannoroth's broken spear still floats above the canyon. Yet the Legion never wholly left. Searing infernals, felguards and mannoroc lashers roam Felfire Hill, the canyon and the ridge above it under the dreadlords Gorgannon and Diathorus the Seeker, and the ancient Gnarl hopes seedlings planted on the hill will one day grow to fight them.

title: Bough Shadow
body: At the far northeastern edge of Ashenvale, just beyond Forest Song, a great tree shelters one of the portals into the Emerald Dream. Green dragonkin stand guard over it: Emeraldon oracles walk with boughguards and tree warders, while the dragons Phantim and Dreamstalker keep close to the portal. None of them welcome visitors. At times the great green dragon Ysondre herself emerges here, crying that the strands of life have been severed and calling on the Dreamers to come forth and take their vengeance.

title: Raene Wolfrunner
body: Raene Wolfrunner is a Sentinel officer in Astranaar, never far from her wolf Dagri. She came from Darnassus by way of Auberdine to deal with the furbolgs of Ashenvale, and she knows these forests as though they were part of her, though they still hide much danger. Sentinel Selarin, who calls her mistress, sends recruits down from Darkshore, and old Thundris Windweaver of Auberdine sends help too, though she is quick to recall that it was she who pulled him from harm's way. She sends hunters against the Thistlefur and Foulweald tribes, and when her friend Teronis failed to return from his search for an old wizard's rod, she took up his cause.

title: Delgren the Purifier
body: Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin who has made his home among the night elves at Maestra's Post, lending his strength wherever the Sentinels find demons or undead. The ways of the kaldorei were strange to him at first, he admits, but he has come to respect them greatly as allies. He studies his enemies too: against the scoffing of others in his order he learned the orcish tongue, and it let him read the writings of the warlock Ilkrud Magthrull. With his pupil Balthule Shadowstrike watching the Tower of Althalaxx, he leads the hunt for the Cult of the Dark Strand, whose master scorned him for taking it as just another death cult.

title: Kayneth Stillwind
body: Kayneth Stillwind is a night elf druid of Forest Song, long its only resident. He fears that a corruption is moving through Ashenvale, and he gathers reports such as Shindrell Swiftfire's to find its trail. Suspecting the Forsaken of spreading disease through the lands of his people, he had a bottle stolen from their camp near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den and tested it himself. The poison attacked his mind, but he resisted, and in his struggle he saw a vision of the barrow's druids murdered by the undead and torn from their bodies. He also sought the Chalice of Elune, an old relic of the shrine now called Satyrnaar, hoping its power might rejuvenate the wounded forest.

title: Krolg
body: Krolg is an old furbolg of the Foulweald tribe who lives alone on the high ground near Mystral Lake, one of the few of his kind untouched by the fel moss that has maddened the tribes. He was cast out of his tribe as the corruption took hold, and he blames the night elves for it, sure that their pride brought ruin on his people. Yet his hatred has limits. He wishes no harm on elven children, and he holds that the furbolgs must answer for their own evils, chief among them the power hungry Ran Bloodtooth. Only a visitor in furbolg shape could ever earn his trust, and he would gladly meet his own kind again in gentler times.

title: Vindicator Vedaar
body: Vindicator Vedaar of the Hand of Argus oversees, with Architect Nemos, the draenei who have come to Forest Song at the night elves' invitation. He carries his people's long memory of flight: the Burning Legion all but destroyed the draenei, and again and again they fell back before it, finding a new home only for the demons to come once more. In Ashenvale he means to stop running. The Legion's remnant on Felfire Hill and in the Demon Fall country to the south is to him an evil that must be cleansed, and when captured plans revealed a demonic assault aimed at Forest Song, he swore by the Seven Crystals of Ata'mal that it would never come to pass.

title: Talen
body: Talen is a night elf drawn by the drowned city of Zoram. He was skimming over its sunken ruins in his small boat when naga surged from the water and set upon him, and he fled ashore with what supplies he could carry, losing his most prized possession on the way: an ancient statuette, the very reason he had braved the Zoram Strand. He believes it holds many of the old city's secrets. When found, it proved to be locked, and only the Ring of Zoram, which belonged to the city's rulers and said to open any lock within it, could open it. The naga leader Ruuzel had found the ring first.

title: Senani Thunderheart
body: Senani Thunderheart is a tauren hunter of Splintertree Post who welcomes young newcomers to what she calls a new frontier, a land full of chances for them to prove their mettle. To her the call of the hunt is something heard from deep within, and it comes from deep within every one of us, if only we listen closely. She keeps the Ashenvale Hunt, a trial against three legendary beasts of the forest, hoping that those who take it up will learn something about themselves along the way. She greets each trophy with praise and promises that songs of the hunters' deeds will be sung at campfires and lumber mills across Ashenvale.

title: Je'neu Sancrea
body: Je'neu Sancrea is a troll shaman of the Earthen Ring at Zoram'gar Outpost, a student of the elements so absorbed in reading the waves that he sometimes fails to notice the people around him. The elements, he teaches, share knowledge that must be learned and secrets that must be kept. When a befouled globe of water was brought to him from Mystral Lake, he recognized it as one of the devices through which powerful elementals draw their strength, and found its taint deeply disturbing. He suspects the Twilight's Hammer of corrupting Baron Aquanis, an elemental power in the nearby depths of Blackfathom, where the cult and the naga have joined forces, and he watches those depths from Zoram'gar.

title: Karang Amakkar
body: Karang Amakkar of Zoram'gar Outpost greets every arrival to what he calls the front lines of the Horde's conquest of Ashenvale. He thinks in routes and gaps. Thistlefur Village blocks a path between Zoram'gar and Splintertree Post that would let the Horde go around Astranaar altogether, so he sends warriors to thin the furbolgs there. Against the Foulweald tribe southeast of Astranaar he planned a show of force: his banner planted on their totem mound and held until their chief, Murgut, came out to save face and fell. The Horde is not to be trifled with, he says, and its conquest of the forest is now in full swing.

title: Ilkrud Magthrull
body: Ilkrud Magthrull is an orc warlock who makes the Fire Scar Shrine of southwestern Ashenvale his home, among felguards and felslayers. Delgren the Purifier knew of him but counted him little more than an annoyance, until the hunt for the Cult of the Dark Strand pointed to him. He fights crying out for the Dark Strand and promising to bleed his foes dry, and his tome, scrawled in Orcish, recorded where the cult's master Athrikus Narassin had hidden his last soul gems. Athrikus himself boasted that orcs and trolls were the easiest of all to win to the cult, so ready was their hatred of the Alliance.

title: Raene's Cleansing
body: Raene Wolfrunner's friend Teronis had gone looking for a way to slow the furbolg attacks: the rod of Dartol, a human wizard who learned druidic magic and used it to move among the furbolgs in their own shape, until they caught him turning tribe against tribe, killed him and broke the rod in three. Teronis was found dead on the island shrine in Lake Falathim, cut down by murlocs, but his journal survived and the gem he sought was won back from them. The dryad Shael'dryn knew the rest. The shaft lay in a chest near Felwood whose key a corrupted treant carried, and the pommel had been given to the druids of Dor'Danil, now dead. Shael'dryn rebuilt the rod, and a hidden shrine in the hills restored its power. In furbolg form its bearer found Krolg, who asked that Ran Bloodtooth, the fiercest of the corrupted, be slain. Raene set his skull and the rod in a place of honor.

title: A Cure for Relara
body: In Astranaar a child named Relara Whitemoon fell gravely ill, and the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf of Maestra's Post sensed that her sickness was more than one of the body. He sent for Bathran's Hair, a plant of the old ruins to the north known to cure ailments of the spirit, and was troubled to learn that the Forsaken now walked there. His cure slowed the illness but did not end it, so her father Pelturas turned to the other remedies Orendil had named. Elune's Tear, a stone found only on the isle of Iris Lake, stirred into a stew, eased her nightmares. Frosted dust from the Ruins of Stardust, made into a poultice, broke her fever. Last came a moonstone from Fallen Sky Lake, taken from the Shadethicket Oracle who hoarded them, and crushed into a cup of tea. Relara woke hungry and asking to go out and play, and her father wept for joy.

title: The Soul Gems of Athrikus
body: When Balthule Shadowstrike's warning reached Maestra's Post, Delgren the Purifier already knew the Cult of the Dark Strand as a thorn in his side, for he had been fighting its members at the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. One of them carried a soul gem that he believed held the secret of the cult's power. Broken open, it gave up a trapped spirit, and what Delgren learned from it pointed to Ilkrud Magthrull, the orc warlock of the Fire Scar Shrine. Ilkrud fell, and Delgren, who had learned to read Orcish despite his order's scorn, found in his tome that the cult's master Athrikus Narassin still kept two soul gems, hidden in the satyr camps of Night Run and Satyrnaar. Freeing the Highborne souls bound inside them broke much of Athrikus's power. Delgren wondered whether the satyrs had been left in the forest too long, then sent his champion north to Balthule for the final blow. When word came that Athrikus was dead, he gave his blessing.
sources: quests 970, 973, 1140, 1167, 981 descriptions and reward texts

title: The Branch of Cenarius
body: The dryad Illiyana of Forest Song was frantic. Her sisters had gone to take the Branch of Cenarius back from the satyrs, searching for the ruins of a night elf temple at Xavian, and two days had gone by without a word. Anilia, who led them, was found near the ruins with a gaping wound in her side. Drawing her rescuer close, she pointed toward an arch to the north and gasped out the name of the one who had taken it: Geltharis. Then she died. The satyr paid for the branch with his life, and it was carried back into dryad hands. Illiyana could scarcely believe the news, for only the day before, she said, she and Anilia had been running and playing in the woods together. Struggling with a sorrow she hardly understood, she asked one thing more: the horns of the satyrs who had taken her sister, so that Anilia's spirit might be gladdened.
sources: quests 1021, 1031, 1032 descriptions, request and reward texts
notes: verified. Faction 1: AllowableRaces 1101.

title: The Scythe of Elune
body: Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow had taken up the work of the priestess Velinde Starsong, who once held the demons of Felwood back from Ashenvale before her efforts faltered and she vanished. To learn why wolf-men had overrun the Shrine of Mel'Thandris, Melyria sent a reader to its tome, and its visions showed that Velinde had received something called the Scythe of Elune. Velinde's own journal, kept with her belongings in Darnassus, told the rest. The scythe, a gnarled branch perhaps older than the kaldorei, weakened the barriers of time and space, and through it she reached the worgen and drew them into the world to fight the demons. At first they served her well. Then a pack vanished, and their numbers kept growing even when she summoned no more. Hearing whispers that a Kirin Tor wizard named Arugal had also called worgen, she sailed from Ratchet to seek him. Her trail led across the sea to Booty Bay, where a caravan driver recalled parting with her on the road north, bound for Darkshire.

title: The Ashenvale Hunt
body: Heralds in Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff, and the hunter Jorn Skyseer in the Barrens, send young warriors north to Splintertree Post, where Senani Thunderheart keeps the Ashenvale Hunt. Three legendary beasts make up the hunt, each a test of cunning and might. The great bear Ursangous, credited with many kills, roams near the Talondeep Path, and a small crescent emblem on his paw suggests he was trained by the night elves. The nightsaber Shadumbra was so savage that every trip west toward the Zoram Strand was fraught with danger. The hippogryph Sharptalon long terrorized peons travelling from the lumber camps to the post. Senani greets each trophy with praise, and the one who brings down all three is hailed as a true hunter, with a gift to mark the deeds done for the Horde.

title: The Befouled Waters
body: The caravans between Splintertree Post and Stonetalon had come to a standstill, for Mystral Lake had come alive and its water elementals were attacking anyone on the way to the Talondeep Path. Mastok Wrilehiss, who has little love for anyone, sent help to clear them, and asked that a gazebo on the lake be scouted too, since it looked straight over the Alliance camp and might serve as a quiet watch post. Among the slain elementals, one left behind a glowing globe of foul water. Mastok had no idea what to make of it, but it gave him a thought: the Earthen Ring. At Zoram'gar, Je'neu Sancrea found the globe deeply disturbing. Powerful elementals draw their strength through such devices, and to find one so tainted spoke of a corruption of the elements themselves, one the Earthen Ring would have to study if it was ever to be ended.

title: The Warsong Lumber Camp
body: Nowhere is the struggle for Ashenvale plainer than at the Warsong Lumber Camp. At Forest Song, Sentinel Luciel Starwhisper calls it a blight: every time her people slow the logging, Overseer Gorthak drives his crews harder, and they now fell more wood than they can use and leave it to rot. She sends fighters against Gorthak, his shredders, deforesters and scouts, while Architect Nemos, who will not cut the grove's ancient trees, has the camp's lumber carried off for Gnarl to purify. Her reports go on to Sentinel Farsong at Silverwing Grove, who directs the wider fight against the Horde. At Splintertree the same camp looks very different. Locke Okarr scrambles to keep it supplied with saw blades from Ratchet, axes from Booty Bay, rope stolen by furbolgs and oil seized by satyrs for their rituals, and Gurda Ragescar hunts for the wind-scattered pages of a shredder manual, unable to get back to work without them.

title: The Dreadlords of Demon Fall
body: The demons of Felfire Hill, Demon Fall Canyon and Demon Fall Ridge are a remnant of a force that invaded the world long ago, and both sides of Ashenvale's war have reason to hate them. At Forest Song, Vindicator Vedaar of the Hand of Argus vows that his people will retreat from the Legion no more. At Splintertree Post the orc Valusha wants the same thing for her own reasons: the demons have been raiding the Warsong Lumber Camp, and they make worthy foes. Each sends fighters against the infernals, felguards and mannoroc lashers, and from the slain came parchments, one in Common and one in Orcish, each telling of an attack in preparation. Two dreadlords command the demons, Gorgannon in the canyon below Mannoroth's floating spear and Diathorus the Seeker in a barrow den atop the ridge, and they were preparing to attack both Forest Song and Splintertree Post. Without them, the demons below would be all but mindless.

title: The Deeps of Blackfathom
body: Near the northern end of the Zoram Strand lies Blackfathom Deeps, long ago a great temple of Elune that held a powerful moonwell. Then the corruption of an Old God seeped up from beneath the earth and fouled the well, and Aku'Mai, a servant of the Old God, rose from its waters. Now the Twilight's Hammer has joined the naga there. The Argent Dawn in Darnassus sent the scout Thaelrid, who learned that the cultists' leader, Twilight Lord Kelris, was sacrificing innocents to Aku'Mai for power. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper wanted brain stems from its satyrs and naga, fearing the blood elves were headed for the same deformity. The Horde came too. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sought the sapphires the naga were harvesting, a fathom core holding the record of elemental activity in the ruins, and the cultist Lorgus Jett, who meant to use the crystals to call back Aku'Mai and the rule of the Old Gods.
